subject.title: [Bug]: claude-cli backend SIGKILLs entire process tree at turn end — Workflow / background tool orphans have no opt-out

question: Should claude-cli live-session cleanup remain unconditional at turn end, or should OpenClaw add a bounded drain or telemetry/failure-signal contract for in-flight CLI-owned background grandchildren?
rationale: The current and shipped source confirm the reported cleanup-to-process-tree-kill behavior, but changing it affects orphan prevention, process lifetime, model-visible terminal state, and likely config/default surfaces.

options.title: Bounded drain plus signal
options.body: Add a narrow owner-approved contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing forced cleanup to the parent/session.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep unconditional cleanup for now, but snapshot, log, or surface killed descendants so the silent failure class becomes observable before changing lifecycle behavior.

options.title: Keep cleanup as contract
options.body: Document that Claude CLI Workflow/Bash grandchildren are not supported across turn boundaries and route users to OpenClaw exec/process or detached task surfaces instead.

recommendation.title: Bounded drain plus signal
recommendation.body: Add a narrow owner-approved contract for detecting in-flight CLI-owned background children, deferring cleanup only within a bounded ceiling, and surfacing forced cleanup to the parent/session.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the strongest recent history on the Claude live-session lifecycle code where this policy decision would likely land.
